we have used WMAP temperature anisotropy maps to constrain the running of the non-Gaussianity parameter f(NL)(=f(NL)(k=k(piv))) to be n(f) = 0(1.2)(1.9), and that the constraints on the running depend somewhat on the choice of prior probabilities assigned to n(f) and f(NL).

we have used WMAP data to constrain the scale-dependence of the local non-Gaussianity parameter f(NL)(fNL) = f(NL)(0)(k/k(piv)(-n(f)(NL)), where k(piv) = 0:002 Mpc(-1) and f(NL)(-1) = 2.5(-0.5)(+0.5) x 10(-4).
the amplitude of the local non-Gaussianity is fNL=0.9+/-5.0 (95% CL), and that the first constraint on its running is n(f)(NL)=0.3(-1.2, +1.9)(95% CL).

the study of non-Gaussianities in the cosmic microwave background.

we have found that the running of non-gaussianity is constrained to be less than 3.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the running of non Gaussianity is a useful parameter for constraining models.

the scale dependence of non-Gaussianities is a useful tool for discriminating between models of inflation, and that the current observational limits on f(NL) are already beginning to probe the scale-dependence of the non-Gaussianity amplitude.

, in the near future, we should expect to be able to constrain the running of nonGaussianity to the point where we can distinguish between models with and without running, which will allow us to distinguish between different inflationary models that produce nonGaussianity.
